hook_text: 2 m 8 cm or 2 m 35 cm: which jump wins? It is not the one with the 8.
clip_script: Sports day in Ladysmith. Ruler for the pencil: line up the 0 mark, not the edge. 12 cm and 4 mm, that is 124 mm. Metre stick for the door. Tape measure for the long jump. Trundle wheel for the track: click, click, 100 clicks, 100 metres. Long jump results: 2 m 35, 2 m 8, 1 m 98, 2 m 50. Metres first: 1 m 98 is shortest. Then centimetres: 8, 35, 50. 2 m 8 cm is shorter than 2 m 35 cm. Pick the tool, start at zero, write the unit.
visual_style: A ruler sliding into place on the 0 mark, then a trundle wheel clicking along a track, then jump distances lining up in order.
mood: Energetic and precise, like sports day officials with clipboards.
pacing: Tools in quick succession, then the long jump twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure three things at home with the right tool.
